schema_note: Curated from official/government-linked sources. Each scheme carries its own source_urls and last_verified date. Detailed rules change over time and vary by state, so the app always tells farmers to confirm final eligibility on the official portal before applying.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
schemes.short_description: Direct income support of Rs 6,000 per year paid to landholding farmer families in three equal installments of Rs 2,000 every four months, transferred straight to the farmer's Aadhaar-linked bank account.
schemes.benefits: Rs 6,000 per year per farmer family, paid as three installments of Rs 2,000 (April-July, August-November, December-March) via Direct Benefit Transfer.

eligibility.notes: Land must be recorded in the applicant's own name (or family member's) in state land records. e-KYC is mandatory to receive installments.

schemes.application_mode: Online self-registration at pmkisan.gov.in, or through the local Common Service Centre (CSC) / Patwari / Revenue Officer.

schemes.name: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana)
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
schemes.short_description: Crop insurance scheme that pays farmers for crop loss or damage from natural calamities, pests and diseases, at a low, fixed premium share while the government subsidizes the rest.
schemes.benefits: Farmer pays only a small share of the premium - 2% of sum insured for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops (which includes tomato); the balance premium is shared by the central and state governments. Claim payouts cover losses from drought, flood, hailstorm, pests/disease and post-harvest damage in a 14-day window.

applicable_crops: notified crops in notified areas, including horticultural crops such as tomato where notified by the state
eligibility.notes: Voluntary for all farmers since 2020. Loanee farmers with a Kisan Credit Card / crop loan may be enrolled automatically unless they opt out; non-loanee farmers must apply. Only crops notified by the state for that season/district are covered, so tomato coverage depends on the state's notification.

schemes.application_mode: Online at pmfby.gov.in, or through your bank, Common Service Centre (CSC), or insurance company agent, within the notified enrolment window for the season.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
schemes.administering_body: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, with NABARD and participating banks
schemes.short_description: A revolving credit line for farmers to fund crop cultivation, inputs and allied activities, at a concessional interest rate, with flexible withdrawal and repayment tied to the cropping cycle.
schemes.benefits: Short-term crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh (being raised to Rs 5 lakh under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme) at an effective interest rate as low as 4% p.a. after a 2% interest subvention plus a 3% prompt-repayment incentive from the government. Collateral-free for loans up to Rs 1.6 lakh. Also carries personal accident insurance and crop-damage insurance cover.

eligibility.notes: Individual owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and SHGs/Joint Liability Groups of farmers are all eligible. Card validity is 5 years, with the limit reviewed annually.

required_documents: Proof of land holding / cultivation, certified by revenue authorities
Cropping pattern / area under cultivation details
schemes.application_mode: Apply at any nationalised bank, regional rural bank, cooperative bank, or small finance bank branch; also available via bank net-banking/YONO-style apps.

schemes.name: Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme
schemes.administering_body: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
schemes.short_description: Free soil testing for every land-holding farmer, with a card that reports nutrient status and recommends the right fertilizer dose and crop choices for that specific field.
schemes.benefits: Free soil sample testing and a printed/digital Soil Health Card every 3 years, showing nutrient levels (N, P, K and micronutrients) and tailored fertilizer/crop recommendations to cut input costs and improve yield.

eligibility.notes: Open to all land-holding farmers with no defined eligibility ceiling; tenants and sharecroppers can also apply where permitted locally.

schemes.application_mode: Register online at soilhealth.dac.gov.in ('Farmer Corner') or through your local agriculture office / Krishi Vigyan Kendra, which will schedule soil sample collection.

schemes.name: PM-KUSUM (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan)
schemes.administering_body: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India
schemes.short_description: Helps farmers move off diesel pumps to solar power - subsidised standalone solar irrigation pumps, solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps, and support to set up small solar power plants on farmland.
schemes.benefits: Central Financial Assistance of 30% of the solar pump/plant cost (Component B/C), with states typically adding their own top-up subsidy on top - total subsidy commonly ranges from 30% to 90% of project cost depending on the state, cutting diesel/electricity costs for irrigation. Component A lets farmers earn income by selling surplus solar power to the grid.

eligibility.notes: Individual farmers, groups of farmers (SHGs/JLGs), cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs and Water User Associations are all eligible. Exact subsidy share and application windows vary by state - check your state's renewable energy nodal agency.

required_documents: Existing electricity connection details (for pump solarisation)
schemes.application_mode: Apply through your state's renewable energy development agency portal (linked from pmkusum.mnre.gov.in) during the state's open application window.
schemes.helpline: State renewable energy agency helpdesk (varies by state)

schemes.name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
schemes.administering_body: Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
schemes.short_description: A pan-India online trading portal that links mandis (APMC markets) so farmers can get transparent, real-time price discovery and sell produce to buyers beyond their local mandi.
schemes.benefits: Access to competitive bidding across linked mandis, real-time commodity prices via app/SMS, quality assaying, and direct online payment settlement to the farmer's bank account - reducing dependence on local middlemen.

applicable_crops: any produce traded at a linked mandi, including vegetables such as tomato where the local mandi is e-NAM enabled
eligibility.notes: Any farmer can register for free; benefit depends on whether your nearest APMC mandi is integrated with e-NAM.

schemes.application_mode: Free registration on the e-NAM portal or mobile app, or through your local APMC mandi office if it is e-NAM linked.

schemes.name: MIDH (Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture)
schemes.administering_body: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India (State Horticulture Missions)
schemes.short_description: Centrally sponsored scheme supporting vegetable and fruit growers - including tomato - with subsidies for quality planting material, protected cultivation (polyhouse/shadenet), micro-irrigation, and post-harvest/cold-chain infrastructure.
schemes.benefits: Project-linked subsidies - for example up to 50% of project cost (capped) for commercial horticulture infrastructure such as polyhouses, and back-ended credit-linked subsidies for quality vegetable seed and planting material; exact percentages vary by component and state, with GOI typically funding 60% and the state 40% of the overall outlay (higher central share for NE/Himalayan states).

eligibility.notes: Open to individual farmers, FPOs and agri-entrepreneurs with agricultural land; specific component eligibility (e.g. polyhouse subsidy) depends on project proposal and state guidelines.

schemes.application_mode: Apply through your District Horticulture Office or the State Horticulture Mission; some components are routed via the National Horticulture Board (nhb.gov.in) for project-based subsidy.
schemes.helpline: District Horticulture Office / State Horticulture Mission
